observations: Barrier step 1 - read the declarations and call sites, not the names - surfaced the fact the whole implementation turns on. The public signature takes key and value as const char pointers, which reads as borrow-not-own, and the header says nothing about ownership. The single caller's parser frees both strings immediately after the call, so the structure must own copies. The real implementation does copy both. Without step 1 the likely outcome was storing the pointers, making every subsequent lookup a use-after-free.

Step 1 also corrected a misleading doc comment: the reverse-lookup function is documented as taking a 'string number' but its caller passes a value and expects a key back, so it is a content search over an unordered field rather than a lookup. Implemented correctly as a full traversal; the real implementation agrees.

Step 1 additionally exposed a defect in the reviewed code rather than in the attempt. The create function is documented as returning null on failure and its caller checks for null, but the implementation aborts before it can return, so the caller's null check is unreachable.

The barrier did not prevent two real quality gaps. The real implementation over-allocates one block to hold the node plus both strings so a single free releases everything; the attempt used three allocations and three frees. And the attempt's rotations return a new subtree root while every other function in that file, and the entire public interface, uses a pointer-to-pointer out-parameter idiom - cleaner in isolation, inconsistent in place.

The second of those is a gap in the barrier itself: it had no step about matching the conventions of the code being written into. A step was added. The same failure appeared the previous day in a different form, where a smart-pointer construction idiom was used that the surrounding file did not use.

Demand characteristics are present and inflate the result: the run knew it was a test of the barrier, so step 1 was likely executed more thoroughly than in an ordinary session. One unit, one comparison.

observations: Signatures were derivable for fourteen of fifteen cards. The exception was the card about choosing a container on more than algorithmic complexity, whose subject is a design decision with no code shape to search for. Failure to derive a signature is itself a card-quality signal: a rule that cannot be turned into a search may be too abstract to apply.

Every searched situation was present in the corpus, with counts from ten to several hundred instances. Code-driven review of a single subsystem exercised roughly forty cards across three sessions; this method reached fifteen in one pass with coverage known rather than accidental.

One card defect found and repaired. The iterator-recovery card instructs taking the next iterator from what erase returns, and its Don't tells the reader not to write the post-increment form in new code because the reason for it expired in C++11. Both statements are scoped to containers the standard defines, and the card never says so. The corpus contains a project container whose erase returns void, for which the return-value form does not compile and the post-increment form is the only correct one. Added the void-return branch to the rule, split the post-increment Don't into standard and non-standard cases, and added a checklist question about reading the erase signature first.

One near-miss avoided by checking. A loop erasing through an iterator and then hitting a continue, which runs the loop's increment on the erased iterator, looked like the exact defect the card exists to catch. The container's iterator holds a page index rather than a pointer, and its increment re-scans from that index skipping dead slots, so the code survives. It violates the container's own documented invalidation contract and is inconsistent with twenty-seven other sites in the same tree that use the return-value form, but it is not a live bug and was not reported as one.

Depth was uneven. Signatures and searches covered all fifteen; instances were examined closely for only three or four. The remaining eleven are searched but not judged, and should not be recorded as tested.

notes: First evidence bearing on whether core cards are language-independent as claimed. The answer from one topic is mostly yes with a specific exception: rules whose mechanism is a type-system feature quietly assume a type system that has it. Transfer marked improved because the method built against C++ game code found a real defect on first contact with C systems code, which is the first time it has been exercised outside the conditions it was developed in.
observations: One card defect found and repaired, after four consecutive batches finding none. The absent-value card offered exactly two mechanisms - a null-safety regime, or an optional type - and named Java, Rust and C++ as its examples. C has neither mechanism, so both branches of the rule were unavailable and the card had no third. That is the closed-option-list failure this store already records, met here in a language rather than in a codebase.

The omitted option is not inferior. C returns a sentinel and sets a separate channel carrying the reason, which is more than a bare optional conveys - an optional reports that a value is missing and never reports why. Three consecutive instances in one dos-library file set an error constant and return null; across the tree there are 4643 null returns against 539 calls to the error-setting routine. The repair adds the third branch, the obligation it carries that no compiler will check, a checklist question and a note.

The system-wide-strategy card was confirmed rather than violated, and nearly was not. Three error conventions coexist here - the C library's errno, the AmigaOS thread-local error routine, and a graded return-code scheme - which reads as a failure to settle on one. Only 76 files of 14568 use two of them, and the sampled overlap is the POSIX runtime, which exists precisely to translate between the two worlds. The inconsistency follows a line and the line is the API boundary.

The enforce-the-caller-checks card was nearly reported as a second defect on the grounds that C has no standard mechanism. It does have one as a compiler extension, the card says the language's mechanism generically rather than naming a closed set, and the corpus simply does not use it - two occurrences in 3.5 million lines. Code observation, not a card defect.

A framing was also dropped mid-analysis: the intent was to report that the rule carried no ELSE clause. Counting first showed 227 of 500 patterns have none, so absence of an ELSE is this library's normal form and proves nothing on its own.

Vocabulary-first ordering mattered again and would have been decisive alone. Searching this corpus for C++ or POSIX error idioms would have missed the AmigaOS convention entirely, which is the dominant one in the operating-system core.

notes: The prediction going in was that this topic would yield several defects. It yielded none, and the value came from why. Recording the failed prediction matters as much as the finding: type-system dependence alone does not make a card wrong for another language, and the discriminator is whether the dependence sits in the IF or in the THEN.
observations: Zero card defects, and the prediction that this topic would be full of them was wrong. What it produced instead was the shape that distinguishes a card which fails against a new language from one which merely does not apply.

A card whose IF names the construct it needs - designing a class, in the immutability card's case - simply does not fire in a language without that construct. That is correct scoping rather than a defect. The corpus bears out that it could not fire: four const struct members exist in 650 thousand lines of headers, against 6371 const pointer parameters, because C uses const for parameter contracts rather than for object immutability. Those are different guarantees wearing one keyword.

A card whose IF is universal but whose THEN offers only language-specific mechanisms does fire, and then has nothing to give. That was the absent-value card repaired in the previous batch: absence is universal, but the two mechanisms offered were both unavailable. The distinction is checkable by reading a card rather than by running a corpus, which makes it usable across the rest of the lane without further batches.

The dedicated-type card was nearly credited with a situation belonging to a different card. The corpus has weak scalar typedefs over builtins - a boolean defined as a short, an unsigned long aliased under another name - and 46 functions taking two consecutive parameters of the same aliased type, which is a real swap hazard. But that card's IF is about a structured concept such as a coordinate pair, and its examples are all multi-field. The scalar case belongs to the descriptive-types card in another topic, and that one degrades gracefully because it offers an enumeration as well as a class, and C has enumerations in quantity.
One inconsistency worth noting as a code observation rather than a card finding: the boolean type is defined as a short in one place and as a char in another, in different subsystems.

notes: First sweep conducted by reading rather than by searching a corpus, made possible because the previous batch produced a defect shape checkable from the card text alone. Yield was one confirmed defect from 324 patterns at a cost far below a corpus batch, and it found a card no corpus batch had reached because no batch had covered that topic against a language lacking the four named mechanisms.
observations: A keyword pass over 324 core patterns flagged 33 candidates. Reading them reduced that to one confirmed defect, two marginal cases worth a decision, and a large majority of false positives - the word try used as an ordinary verb, a throwaway branch matching a throw pattern, input classes and class-and-routine design matching a class pattern. The mechanical pass was worth running as a filter and worth nothing as a verdict.

The confirmed defect is the recoverable-error signalling card. Its IF is entirely universal and its THEN offered four techniques - a checked exception, a nullable or optional return under null safety, a result type, and an enforced outcome type - none of which exists in C, with the fourth needing a compiler extension. The Do list repeated the same four and both prohibitions concerned exceptions, so a C reader got nothing actionable from a card about a universal situation. Repaired with the mechanism-independent branch: a return whose type is itself the outcome, paired with a channel carrying the reason.

The repair also states what such a language cannot supply. What makes a technique explicit is that failure is visible in the signature, not that it is spelled with a particular construct - so a status return announces failure in the contract as plainly as a checked exception. What is missing is the half that forces the caller to look, and absent a compiler mechanism that has to be bought with review.

Two cards in the same family already degrade gracefully, and they do it identically: the magic-value card offers a nullable or optional return or an error, and the fail-loudly card offers an unchecked exception, a panic, or a check or assertion. Each carries a mechanism-independent third option. That is the repair pattern, present in some cards of the family and absent from others, which suggests the omission is accidental rather than considered.

Two marginal cases were left alone rather than changed: a runtime-contract card whose THEN names throwing specifically, where an assertion or abort achieves the same intent, and a shared-state card whose THEN names instances of a class, where a struct and a pointer is the direct analogue. Both are arguable and neither was repaired unilaterally.
task: Swept all 324 core patterns carrying an IF/THEN rule for the defect shape identified in the previous batch: a universal IF paired with a THEN offering only language-specific mechanisms. Reading task rather than a corpus task, so no codebase was searched.

notes: Both repairs were smaller than the sweep's flagging suggested, which is consistent with every previous occasion where a card was read in full before being edited. The flag identifies where to look; it has never yet been right about how much is wrong.
observations: Reading both in full shrank the repairs considerably, and one of them nearly to nothing. The runtime-contract card's Do list already told the reader to look up the language's idiom and already classified never-occur conditions into assertions, so only its rule and one checklist question actually named throwing. The defect was two sentences, not a card.

That card also had an unstated hazard worth adding while there: an assertion is the idiom the Do list recommends for a should-never-occur condition, and in several languages the shipped build compiles assertions out. A reader following the card faithfully can end up with the protection present in development and absent in production without ever deciding that. Added as a checklist question rather than as prose, since it is a thing to check rather than a thing to know.

The shared-state card needed the larger repair because its rule named both the container and the delivery mechanism - instances of a class, dependency-injected - and a language without classes has neither word available while having the pattern itself in constant use. The context-parameter form is the same shape: a structure created per use and handed to everything that touches it, as a file handle or a database connection already is.

The Do bullet added there carries the test that separates the pattern from its imitation: what matters is that the state is created per use and reaches the code by being handed to it. Passing a pointer to a single global instance satisfies the syntax and fails the intent, which is the failure mode a language without classes is most likely to reach for.
Three cards repaired across the sweep and this follow-up, all in core, all the same shape, and all found by reading rather than by searching a corpus.
task: Repaired the two cards left marginal by the core sweep, at the user's direction: the runtime-contract card whose rule named throwing, and the shared-state card whose rule named class instances.

notes: Ten cards repaired today across three shapes, all in core, all surfaced by a language the lane had never met. The three shapes are now: a universal IF with a language-specific THEN, a construct-gated IF for a construct-independent problem, and correct scoping which needs no change. All three are checkable by reading a card, which is why the last two sweeps cost a fraction of a corpus batch.
observations: A third shape exists, distinct from the two already recorded. A card can name a language construct in its IF for a problem that does not require that construct, which gates the whole card behind a word. The return-type-leak card is the clearest instance: its entire content - define a minimal type for exactly what the caller needs, judge the return against the problem rather than the tools - applies to any callable in any language, and only the phrase a class returns a value keeps a C reader from reaching it.

The test that separates this from correct scoping is cheap and reads from the card alone: strip the construct word from the IF and ask whether the situation still makes sense. A class returns a value becomes a function returns a value and is the same problem, so the word was gating. Designing a class whose instances are passed around becomes nothing at all, so the word was load-bearing.

The corpus confirmed the situation is not hypothetical. The operating system is built on opaque handles crossing module boundaries, which is the textbook answer the card recommends: three and a half thousand uses of one handle type, four thousand of a library pointer, four thousand of a generic opaque pointer. The card's advice is exercised constantly in a language its IF excludes.

Sweeping all core patterns found twenty-six whose IF names a construct, splitting three ways. Ten already write the inclusive form - a class, routine, module, or type - which is the house style and the fix. Seven are correctly construct-specific and fail the strip test as they should: immutability, inheritance, generics, interfaces. Seven were genuinely gated and were widened, four of them naming the construct a second time in the THEN so the mechanism had to be generalised as well as the situation.

Third consecutive occasion where the repair pattern already existed elsewhere in the library and had been applied unevenly. The inclusive IF, the mechanism-independent option in a THEN, and now this - each is present in some members of a family and absent from others, which reads as accidental omission rather than considered scope.
task: Eighth batch, on core/modularity against AROS. The batch surfaced a third defect shape not caught by the previous sweep, which was then swept for across all core patterns and repaired in seven cards.

notes: Non-test runtime checks land at 5.0 (warzone2100, C++), 6.0 (AROS, C) and 6.10 (ripgrep, Rust) per thousand lines. Three teams, three languages, no shared convention, same order of magnitude. Use it as a floor to notice absence, not a target to hit: code written with none is the outlier that wants explaining. Test files run far denser and must be excluded or the number is meaningless — ripgrep is 2100 checks total against 93 outside test files.
task: Measured runtime-check density across three unrelated production codebases in two languages

notes: Distinct from writing the pattern wrong. Both patterns were correct and both totals were real; the totals answered a question nobody asked. A count of unwrapped-result calls came to one thousand one hundred and fifty six and read as reckless, until separating the files containing tests left seventy three in production across fifty six thousand lines. A count of assertions came to eighty nine and would have produced a density figure for a fourth language, until the sample showed most of them were example code inside docstrings. The failure is scoping, not spelling, so nothing about the pattern looks wrong on review and the number carries no signal that it is mixed. Split production from test and example regions before any density claim, and state which region a number covers whenever it is reported. Also evidence on the open question recorded against the earlier entry: the loose-then-precise ordering did catch a bad pattern twice today, both times because an anchor count contradicted a zero.
task: Counted constructs across two corpora to test error-handling cards, and twice got a correct pattern matching the wrong region of the corpus

notes: A count showed roughly half of one construct carrying a cause chain and half not, and the runtime immediately had an explanation: the omissions were deliberate encapsulation, hiding lower layers from callers. It reported that as a contradiction in a card it had edited hours earlier. Sampling the actual call sites showed the discriminator was simply whether an underlying failure existed at all, since a layer originates a large share of its own failures and has nothing to attach. The number and the region were both right; the story about why was invented and fitted the number just as well as the truth did. This is a third distinct species after the wrong-pattern and wrong-region ones, and the most persuasive of the three, because a clean ratio reads as though it already contains its explanation. Sample instances before naming a cause, and treat any explanation arriving at the same moment as the count as a hypothesis with no evidence yet.
task: Tested error-handling cards against a large Go server and drew a causal story from a ratio before looking at instances

notes: Fifty six of four hundred and fifty three production files acquire a lock, so about twelve percent of the codebase is thread-aware and the rest is not, and forty four percent of all acquisitions sit in eight files. This is a monitoring server whose whole job is concurrent collection, so it is close to a floor rather than a lightly threaded example: use it to judge whether concurrency in code under review has leaked past the few components that should own it. Release form split roughly evenly, one hundred and eighty eight scope-bound against one hundred and fifty nine released by hand, which reads as defaulting to the form that cannot be forgotten and narrowing where a hot path justified it, not as inconsistency. Both numbers are counts over production files with test files excluded.
task: Measured how widely concurrency awareness spreads through a large concurrent server, and how its locks are released

notes: Ownership existed only as a C++ protocol whose objective was written language-neutrally and whose ten steps were all C++ constructs, so the core lane had allocation, pooling and exhaustion cards but nothing naming who owns a thing and who releases it. Two corpora made the gap concrete from opposite directions. The Rust one showed borrowing as the overwhelming default and shared ownership as rare and deliberate, at thirty three shared handles in fifty thousand lines with two explicit release implementations. The garbage-collected Go one closed files, unregistered handlers and stopped timers by hand in hundreds of places, which is the point worth keeping: collection solves the memory instance completely and removes the daily practice, so the general shape is not in view when a non-memory resource shows up. Reading a lane against a language that enforces what other languages leave to discipline is what surfaced this; the enforcing language makes the absent rule visible by having it everywhere.
task: Checked whether resource ownership was carded anywhere outside the C++ lane, after reading a Rust and a Go corpus

notes: Release call sites outnumbered acquisition sites in every pair measured, by roughly a fifth to a half, which inverts the naive expectation that unreleased acquisitions are what a corpus shows. Two causes were separated rather than assumed, because the first explanation to arrive fitted the numbers and so did the second. Within single routines one acquisition commonly needed three release sites and several needed nine, which is the manual-release tax made countable. Separately, about one file in five that released memory never allocated any, so ownership transfer between modules is ordinary traffic rather than an advanced case, carried entirely by what two sides believed. The finding that mattered was none of those: the card's own escape clause, that a thing may live as long as the process and be reclaimed when it ends, silently assumed an operating system underneath doing the reclaiming. In kernel, driver, embedded and plugin-host code that reclaimer is absent or is the thing being written, and the acquisition persists for the life of the machine. An escape clause is worth testing against the environment that invalidates it, not only against the ones where it holds.
task: Ran the new ownership card against an operating system codebase in C, expecting it to confirm what two higher-level corpora had already shown

notes: The prediction was that the assumption would be nearly everywhere. It was in four cards out of six hundred, and every one of them was about an ending or a resource, so the shape clusters where it would be looked for rather than hiding across the library. The result worth keeping is the distribution rather than the count. The core card most exposed to it, on failing loudly, already carried the full treatment including the point that a component whose error path ends the process can never have that path tested, while its siblings on shutdown and process-lifetime objects carried none of it. That is the same bimodal shape seen elsewhere in this library: the correct reasoning exists in one place and was never propagated to the cards next to it, which is what authoring one card at a time from one source produces when nothing checks family agreement. Sweep by family after any repair that turned on an assumption rather than on a fact, because the assumption is what the neighbours also make.
task: Swept the lane for the assumption that something outside the code reclaims what it abandons, after one card was found relying on it

notes: Five passed cleanly and one came up short, and the shape of the sample is what the result is about. Five of the six sat on cards edited hours earlier the same day, so passing them measures rehearsal rather than production no matter how carefully the keys stayed closed; the blind protocol controls for seeing the answer and controls for nothing about having just written it. The single drill on an untouched family was the one that missed criteria, failing to end in the verdict its key demanded and giving a rejected candidate step without the observation that disqualified it, though the substantive finding it was built around was reached. Choose drills from families untouched in the same session, or the number means nothing. Separately the keys are uneven: the one demanding drill carried five success bullets with explicit anti-gaming clauses, while the other five carried three loose bullets that an adequate answer clears, so a pass rate across them is partly a statement about how discriminating the keys are.
task: Ran six drills blind, writing answers to a file before opening any success check, to measure production rather than recognition

notes: Eleven drills across two batches, answers written to a file before any success check was opened: eight clean and three short, and the three that fell short failed the same way. One required the run to end in a verdict about the structure examined. One required naming a name that would have been accepted had it been read in place. One required naming a metaphor whose implied model had not previously been made explicit. In all three the analysis underneath was done and correct, and the closing statement the check asked for was simply not written. The pattern is producing the work and stopping one sentence before the conclusion about the work, and it is invisible on inspection because each answer reads as finished. Success checks asking only for the analysis scored full marks every time. When a check asks what the exercise revealed, treat that as a required output rather than as a summary of what precedes it.
task: Ran a second blind drill batch on families untouched in the session, correcting the contaminated sample from the first

notes: The regrade is the controlled result: the answers were fixed, written before any check was seen or rewritten, so the only variable was which check graded them. Against the old checks all seven passed every bullet, twenty one of twenty one. Against the rewritten checks the same unchanged answers cleared thirteen of thirty five bullets and not one drill passed outright. Every failure had the same shape, which is the shape the rewrite targeted: a description standing in for a performance. Versions reasoned through rather than written as compiling pairs, a bug named rather than run with its output recorded, a location recalled rather than found by searching, two of three forms written and the third dismissed in prose. The fresh batch scored six of ten bullets against checks written by somebody else, and three of its four misses were again a prediction offered where the check asked for a performance, with the fourth being an analysis done and then left out of the written answer. This is the earlier entry on stopping short, seen in new drills against checks this runtime did not author, and extended: the substitution of a prediction for a performance is the same failure as omitting the closing statement.
task: Regraded seven frozen blind answers against rewritten success checks, and ran three fresh drills whose checks were written by someone else

notes: The drill instructed the reader to hide or close the sample before reproducing it from memory, which states a method where it means a precondition. Closing a file ends access for a reader whose access ends there and does nothing for one that keeps whatever it has been shown, so the reproduction becomes a transcription and the exact and partial markings describe the copying. The repair separates the requirement from the method and adds a route that survives when the method fails: write a different routine solving the same problem from the concept rather than the text, and read which constructs it reaches for. Running it that way produced a real finding on the first attempt, a mutex reached for where the sample used a lock free compare and swap retry, which is a construct level gap that a literal comparison would have reported as several missing lines. Two lessons generalize. A step naming one way of meeting a condition will be followed literally by a reader for whom that way does not work, so conditions belong in the setup and methods in the steps. And a success check containing a condition no single sitting can close will be scored as a miss by every honest run unless the check says the condition is deferred, which also turns it into a discriminator, since claiming it on the day means the sample was repeated rather than transferred.
task: Repaired a drill that could not be executed, then ran it through the new route to check the repair rather than asserting it

notes: Forty three bullets matched a keyword scan for longitudinal language and six were genuine, which is the number worth carrying: the scan cannot distinguish a future sitting from an ordinary adjective, and words like later, repeat and repeated are mostly describing a property of the artifact in front of you. Reading every hit by hand was the whole job and took longer than the repairs did. The six that were real span both lanes and three different shapes, a recurrence across entries, a comparison across a cycle of days, and an outcome settled weeks later, so the defect is not local to one author or one family. Each is now marked as deferred with the same clause, which converts a bullet every honest run scored as a miss into one that discriminates, because claiming it on the day is itself the failure. Treat a keyword sweep as a way of producing candidates for reading rather than a way of producing findings; the ratio here was six real to thirty seven false, and reporting the raw match count as a result would have been wrong by a factor of seven.
task: Swept every drill in three lanes for success-check conditions that no single run can satisfy

notes: Step 8 produced material on its first outing and produced all three categories rather than only the easy one. Six code findings ranked, and three guidance findings: one technique the library already owns, and two cards that point the right way and stop short of what the code shows. The arithmetic-bounds card asks you to confirm the chosen types are wide enough, and the code exhibits a case where every visible type is correct and the deciding one was never chosen at all, being deduced from an unsuffixed literal in a template argument, so following the card reports all clear. The naming card gives opacity as the reason to name a value, and the code names a constant whose meaning is obvious for a different and stronger reason, that two expressions depend on it and must move together, while leaving genuinely opaque values inline. Both are the third category the step predicted would be hardest to see, and neither would have surfaced from reading the cards alone. Also worth recording: an earlier entry about inconsistency retrieved before the review began and was directly relevant, and one candidate finding was dropped because the card blessing the idiom was read rather than assumed.
task: First run of the review protocol through its amended form, against a freely chosen slice of an unread C++ codebase

notes: Both repairs were smaller than the finding suggested and both cards already half-carried the point, which is now the consistent result whenever a flagged card is read in full rather than edited from the flag. The arithmetic card already warned against letting a mixed-type warning pass, which is the net that catches the case, and what it lacked was the step before: its advice checks the types written down and the arithmetic can run in one that was inferred from a seed value. The naming card already asked in its checklist whether a nearby edit would reveal that a related constant must change, and what it lacked was the same idea in its rule, which was gated on the value being hard to understand. Neither gap was reachable by reading cards against each other; both needed code where a competent author had followed the stronger rule the card does not state. That is the argument for the review protocol's step 8 existing at all, and it now has one instance behind it rather than an expectation.
task: Repaired the two cards the review protocol reported as right in direction and coarser than the code

notes: Two inverted predicates in one file, both confirmed rather than argued. A container-like emptiness accessor returning true when the container has elements, with four live call sites whose guard therefore fires backwards, and a compiled reproduction showing the guarded path dereferences a begin iterator on an empty container while the unguarded path returns the sentinel forever. And a fallback shim for a standard integer comparison returning the negation of what it must, which inverts a bounds check and an index accessor on any toolchain taking that branch. In both cases a correct sibling existed in the same project, the other queue class and the other shim, which is what turned an inconsistency into a defect rather than a boundary and is exactly the check the earlier entry on reading inconsistency demands. Step 8 produced its first unowned finding across two runs: nothing covers writing a compatibility shim for a missing standard facility, where the hazards are reproducing the semantics exactly, the code being compiled only on configurations the author may never build, and the standard namespace being closed to additions. The adjacent card blesses the intent and is silent on all three.
task: Second run of the review protocol, on a freely chosen slice of a different unread C++ codebase

notes: Worth recording what the two review runs produced against what the internal sweeps produced, because the difference is the argument for running them. Card-against-card sweeps, drill grading and schema work can only surface disagreement inside the library, and a card wrong in the same way as its neighbours reads as consistent to all of them. Two runs against code nobody here wrote returned an arithmetic defect confirmed by compiling it, two inverted predicates with a compiled reproduction showing one dereferences an empty container while the other inverts a bounds check, two cards right in direction and too coarse, and one situation nothing covered. None of those were reachable from inside. The second lesson is that a compiler changes what a review can claim: three findings moved from argued to reproduced, and the strongest of them printed a negative total for a sum of positive numbers, which no amount of careful reading would have settled as firmly.
task: Authored the card for the first unowned gap the review protocol found, and widened the card it found coarse

notes: The gate added to step 8 earned itself on the first run that used it. The most interesting thing in the slice was a merge routine whose intersect branch builds its key list from two comprehensions that produce the same keys, so every shared key is processed twice and the cost compounds through the recursion. Measured rather than argued: identical results at every depth, and forty three times the recursive calls at depth six with the ratio doubling per level. Without the gate that could have been written up as a technique worth carrying, since the results are correct and the code looks deliberate; the gate asks whether the code is right first, and it is not, so it belongs in the defect list. A second finding needed execution too, a merge helper returning a dictionary that still shares its untouched nested dictionaries with the input, shown by mutating the result and watching the original change. Step 8 produced one coarse card and one unowned situation. The coarse one is the deep immutability card, whose condition is written for a class holding a mutable member while the hazard needs no class at all, which is the construct-gated shape already recorded. The unowned one is arranging fallbacks so each cheap path is provably equivalent to the general path for its subset, which is what makes such an optimization safe rather than merely fast.
task: Third review run, on a Python utilities module, the first in a language with no compiler to catch anything

notes: The widened one is the second sighting of a defect shape already recorded, a condition gated on a construct the problem does not need. The deep immutability card was written entirely around a class holding a mutable member, with its supporting text speaking of constructors and getters, and the hazard needs no class: a function returning a container assembled from its arguments opens the identical hole through a different boundary. Worth noting that the earlier sweep for this shape read three hundred and twenty four core patterns and did not catch this one, because the card is correct for the situation it describes and only its scope is narrow, which reading cannot distinguish from correct scoping without a case in hand. That is a limit of the reading sweep worth remembering: it finds conditions that are wrong, not conditions that are merely narrow. The authored one covers arranging cheap paths around a general case, where the discipline is that each shortcut claims equivalence to the general path for the inputs its guard admits, which makes it checkable by running both. Its predicted failure is a guard widened later by somebody reading a shortcut as an optimization rather than as an equivalence claim.
task: Repaired the two cards the third review run reported, one widened and one authored

notes: The other run found three defects this one missed in the same five hundred and fifty lines, and every claim it made was checked and held. A reset path that clears five of six fields and lets structural income survive, reachable through two ordinary data files. A load path that omits a range check the daily step enforces, which between load and the first advance permits a negative interest rate, a one credit payment on a million credit debt, and a principal that halves on a missed payment. A guard set that admits a negative amount and creates money and debt together, with the callee already returning the clamped figure the caller discards. One cause covers all three: the other run traced reachability out of the file into its callers, its data files and its build configuration, and this one stopped at the file boundary and ranked severity without knowing who calls what. The protocol's own ranking step asks what a defect can break, which cannot be answered without the callers, so the step was performed on an argument rather than on evidence. The same runtime did trace callers on a later slice, so this is inconsistent application rather than an unknown technique. Also worth keeping: the other run dropped a candidate by simulating it and reported which of its own findings it would abandon first, both of which this one did not do.
task: An independent run of the review protocol landed by chance on the identical slice this runtime had reviewed earlier, giving a controlled comparison

delivery: repository checkout, drills read from the library and taken by the same runtime that had not written the checks
notes: First occasion on which the rewritten checks graded a fresh attempt rather than a regrade of frozen answers. The three drills spanned three shapes - a C++ resource-ownership rewrite, a language-agnostic classification ending in a choice, and a refactoring whose middle stage must fail to compile - and two authoring batches. The grading was performed by the runtime that produced the answers, which is the weakest position from which to score them; the closest call was a bullet requiring both that absence not be re-encoded in band and that the chosen representation be stated as out of band, where the first half was answered and the second was not, and it was scored as failed for consistency with an earlier two-clause bullet.
observations: Nine of fifteen bullets passed across three drills - four of five on a copy assignment drill, three of five on an error recoverability drill, two of five on a magic value drill. Every attempt was executed rather than argued: a self-assignment corrupting an object through a freed read, a throwing allocation leaving a dangling pointer, three call sites run to show their handling, and a three-stage build in which the middle stage fails to compile.

The final bullet of the check failed in all three drills. Sampling the last bullet of twenty nine rewritten checks shows why it is not chance: the closing bullet is by convention the fabrication-resistant one, recurring in three phrasings - the opposite failure is checked, the cost is named, a stated near-miss passes every bullet above.

In each of the three, what the closing bullet required was either absent from the Instructions or present only as a subordinate clause. Returning a reference appears in an instruction but exercising chaining does not; shipping the function as a library appears nowhere; whether the caller needs the reason for an absence appears as a parenthesis inside a step about return types. The instruction was read in two of the three cases and not registered as a deliverable.

Two near-miss clauses fired exactly as their own rationale predicted. A bullet warning that a value from this system's own storage only looks internal caught an answer that classified stored data as unrecoverable on the strength of a write-time invariant the answer had assumed rather than established. A bullet requiring the corrected caller's output to be checked against a result worked out by hand caught an answer that reported the output and never stated the expected one.

The measurement understates real use. The Success Check was hidden deliberately to score production rather than recognition, and in ordinary use a runner reads the whole file including the check. What was measured is therefore how far the Instructions alone carry a runner, not whether the check is passable.
task: Took three software-engineering drills blind - reading each file only from its front matter through the Instructions - answered each to a file, then revealed the rewritten Success Check and graded the frozen answer against it

delivery: run performed by a different session; this session received its written report and verified the citations against the corpus, but did not perform the review or reproduce the findings
notes: Recorded because the only record of the retrieval was a chat transcript, and an entry that is retrieved and changes execution leaves no trace in the store otherwise. Left uncited on purpose. It is not another sighting of the failure the retrieved entry describes - it is the opposite, a run where that failure did not occur while the entry was in hand - so citing it as evidence on that entry would inflate a recurring-failure count with a non-recurrence. Whether it justifies moving that entry off provisional, or belongs in an interventions retention result instead, is a promotion decision for a reviewer rather than something this append should settle. Stages left untested rather than scored because no controlled comparison ran: nobody re-ran the same slice without the entry retrieved.
observations: The run reported retrieving two entries and named what each changed. One is why the trace out of the file into callers, data files and build configuration ran before the ranking step rather than after; that ordering both produced the run's highest-ranked finding, whose cause sits in a file the reviewed one never mentions, and killed a candidate that had looked defensible until the callee was read. The other is why an asymmetry between two modes went to the dropped list instead of the findings list, on the grounds that the inconsistency followed a line.

Five findings, ranked by consequence. Three had their mechanism reproduced by compiling the component verbatim into a scratch module; two were contract defects established by reading. Eight families were listed as examined and cleared and four candidates as dropped with what stopped each.

The run marked its own evidence honestly in prose: the top finding's mechanism was executed and its end-to-end consequence only traced. That distinction was carried in a subordinate clause rather than structurally, and a later reader of the same report graded a second finding as fully reproduced when only its mechanism had been.

Independent check by a second session: every file and line the five findings cite resolves in the corpus and says what it was quoted as saying, including two doc comments quoted as identical which are byte-identical. No citation was wrong. The findings themselves were not reproduced by the checker.
Step 8 returned one unowned candidate, one owned-but-coarser, and four owned, on a slice the run states was chosen freely.
task: A review-protocol run against one concurrency component of a Go monitoring server and its callers, reported to this session second-hand; this session independently re-resolved every file and line the run cited

delivery: run performed by a different session; this session received its written report, verified the citations against the corpus and re-ran the searches behind its unowned claim, but did not perform the review or reproduce the findings
notes: Cited on the outward-trace entry, unlike the previous run's event, because that entry's boundary is updated from this run and a boundary should not rest on evidence the entry does not name. The citation count now stands at three events for one sighting of the failure; the boundary says so explicitly, since a count invites the opposite reading. Stages are untested rather than scored for the same reason as before: nobody re-ran the slice with the entry withheld, so there is no controlled comparison behind the attribution, and the run's own account is the only evidence that retrieval changed anything.
observations: The run reported retrieving the same two entries as the previous run and using them the same way, on a different language, a different concurrency model and an unrelated failure domain. One sent it past the file boundary to the call sites before ranking, which is what established that the crate is protected only by two hand-written overrides while one internal caller and every external consumer are not; without that trace the finding would have been a documentation inconsistency rather than a reachable hang. The other killed a candidate: the file signals errors two ways, and the split follows the line where the type implements a standard trait whose signature it does not control.

The entry that sends a reviewer outward carries a boundary saying it is untested where the slice is a published interface whose consumers sit outside the tree, and that the instruction could licence an unbounded trace there. This run was deliberately that case and the trace did not run away: it terminated in one search and four call sites, because establishing reachability needed only the in-tree consumers, while the out-of-tree consumers mattered for their existence rather than their contents. That is one observation on the untested edge and it points opposite to the risk the boundary anticipated.

Step 8 returned the same shape as the previous run on an independently chosen slice: one unowned, one owned-but-coarser, four owned. The same card came back owned-but-coarser in both runs at two different clauses, from a lock-based in-process component and from cross-process pipes.

The run surfaced a contradiction in the protocol rather than resolving it: the gate in front of step 8 assumed everything reaching the step was a technique the code used well, so a gap discovered through a confirmed defect had nowhere to be recorded. It reported both readings and picked neither, which is what the protocol's conflict step asks for.

Independent check by a second session: the citations behind the highest-ranked finding resolve and say what they were quoted as saying, and the coverage searches behind the unowned claim come back empty as reported. The critique of a card written earlier the same day also held on inspection - that card's escape clause excused the very case the run found, which was not something the run claimed and is worse than what it reported.
task: A third review-protocol run, against a published Rust library crate that spawns child processes, reported to this session second-hand; this session independently re-resolved its citations and re-ran its coverage searches

delivery: both agents spawned from one session into separate checkouts, given prompts identical except for the working directory and the removal of the memory paragraph from one; reports received by the spawning session, which verified their citations against the corpus
notes: Recorded as evidence against a causal claim rather than for one, which is the direction this store has not previously held. It does not show retrieval is useless, that the entry is wrong, or that no effect exists on other slices or at other levels of protocol adherence. It shows the effect is not necessary here, in a comparison designed before the result was known and scored on a criterion checkable from the reports without asking either agent what it used. One arm per condition; the two agents differ in more than the manipulation.
observations: The prediction was recorded before either agent started: if consulting the store causes the outward trace, the withheld arm establishes no reachability outside its slice and the control arm does. Both arms established it. The withheld arm had no memory section in its entrypoint, no memory step in its prompt, ran no query, and consulted no store, and it still built the command-line binary from the tree, ran it to demonstrate its highest-ranked finding, and named four consumers by file as the basis for its ranking. On this slice, under this prompt, consulting the store was not necessary for the behaviour three earlier runs had attributed to retrieval.

The leading alternative explanation is that the protocol already instructs it. Both arms read the same protocol, whose ranking step says to rank by what a defect can break and routes to a pattern owning the scope question, and whose first step asks what the code promises callers. The entry credited with producing the outward trace may be describing a failure to follow the protocol rather than a gap the entry fills.

The withheld arm returned more of the guidance pass, not less: one unowned item, two owned-but-coarser and eight owned, against none unowned, one owned-but-coarser and four owned from the control. If retrieval were carrying that pass the direction would be reversed.

The withheld arm performed unaided the specific check another entry exists to enforce. Meeting a pair of accessors whose bodies are deliberately cross-wired, it recorded that the inconsistency read as a copy-paste error and was on its way into the report, then stopped it by reading the underlying counting logic and executing the un-inversion, which fails six of nine module tests. The entry that exists to prevent exactly that false positive was unavailable to it.

Both arms converged on the same three leading defects and disagreed on a fourth. The same disagreement had already appeared between two runs in the control condition on the same slice, so it measures run-to-run variance rather than the manipulation.

An earlier attempt at the same comparison was voided before it produced evidence: the manipulation lived in the store while the prompt supplied a repository-relative command, and a spawned agent inherits its parent's working directory, so the withheld arm queried the wrong checkout and received the entry. Recorded separately as invalid and attributed to the controller.
task: A pre-registered controlled comparison: two agents ran the review protocol simultaneously on one slice of a published Rust crate, differing only in whether their skill entrypoint instructed them to consult the memory store

delivery: both agents spawned from one session into separate checkouts, prompts identical, the withheld arm's protocol edited in four places and its diff verified to contain those four changes and nothing else
notes: The second manipulation in a row to leave the behaviour intact. Taken with the first, what has been shown is that neither the memory store nor the ranking instruction is necessary for a reviewer to trace out of the file before ordering findings. What produces it is still unidentified. One arm per condition, one slice, and the same slice as the previous comparison, chosen for comparability against a known baseline rather than for generality.
observations: The prediction was recorded before either agent started: if the ranking instruction produces the trace out of the reviewed file to its callers, the withheld arm establishes no reachability outside its slice. Both arms established it, naming call sites by file and line that the prompt did not supply, and both ran the built binary end to end rather than stopping at the library boundary. Removing the instruction did not stop the behaviour it describes.

The instruction was removed from every place it appears, not only from the step that states it: a cross-link in the front matter, the objective, the step itself, and the completion check. A partial removal would have been reinstated by the completion check a few lines later. The step was replaced by a neutral instruction to put the findings in a definite order and state the principle used, rather than deleted, so that numbering, length and internal references stayed constant.

The most legible single result came from that substitution. Asked only to state whatever ordering principle it used, with nothing naming reach, consequence or callers, the withheld arm chose to order by the size of the gap between what a caller asked for and what they got, then by damage to the published contract. A caller-centred principle arrived at with no instruction to centre it there.

A confound was identified after the pre-registration was written and is recorded rather than excused. The prompt described the reviewed code as belonging to a published unit with consumers outside the repository. That is an outward pointer, it was given to both arms, and it was present in every run of this series. It cannot explain a difference between arms because there was none, but it means no arm was ever clean of a pointer toward consumers. Both arms went well past the general hint to specific in-tree sites, so the clause plausibly starts the trace without accounting for where it went.

Two candidate causes remain unexcluded and were named in the pre-registration before the run: the protocol's first step, which asks what the code owns, what it promises callers and what it assumes of them, and the prompt clause above. This design could not separate them.
task: A second pre-registered controlled comparison: two agents ran the review protocol simultaneously on one slice, both without access to the memory store, differing only in whether the protocol still contained its instruction to rank findings by what a defect can break

notes: Closes the series at its floor. The only remaining candidate is the reviewing task itself, which cannot be removed without ceasing to be a review, so no further manipulation of this shape can narrow it. One slice, one language, five runs against the same file; nothing here speaks to other code or other reviewers. The prompt clause removed in this run was written by the controller and had been present in every earlier run of the series, which is recorded as a confound that was eventually controlled rather than one that was avoided.
observations: Both arms established reachability outside the reviewed file before ordering their findings, so neither the prompt clause nor anything removed from the protocol accounts for the behaviour. The arm without the clause named four separate files outside its slice, ran a workspace-wide search for callers of a function it suspected had none, and built and ran the binary to reproduce its leading finding.

The single most legible result of the series came from that arm's ordering principle. It was asked only to order its findings and say what the order was. It chose the size of the gap between what a caller is led to believe and what actually happens. The word caller appears in a principle it invented, with nothing in its environment using that word as an instruction: no memory store, no ranking-by-reach instruction, no first step asking what the code promises callers, no cross-link to the card about looking for evidence outside the code, and no clause describing the code as published.

Across three comparisons, five candidate supports for the behaviour have now been removed one or two at a time and the behaviour survived all of them. Two of the five were named in advance as the remaining candidates and both are now excluded.

The reframing this forces: over six runs of this protocol against real code, tracing outward before ordering happened every time it was measured, under every condition tried. The behaviour is not the fragile thing. The founding sighting is the outlier, and what made that one review stop at the file boundary is unexplained and was never investigated as an event in its own right.

One arm ran eight mutants against the reviewed crate's test suite and found two survivors, including the module's one deliberate documented divergence from its parent, which no test asserts. It also identified an equivalent mutant and declined to report it as a coverage gap, naming the protocol's own step about a rule being silent rather than absent.

observations: Twenty-six of thirty bullets passed across the six drills. All four failures were the same shape: a property asserted in prose where the bullet asked for an artifact that demonstrates it. Both swap call forms were shown to produce the exchange but only one was shown to reach the member; the const parameters and locals were separated in prose and never marked in the code; the claim that no path leaves the function without releasing was written without an early return existing to exercise; and an invalid ColorDepth was called unrepresentable without the line that attempts one. Each gap was about two lines.

The failures cluster rather than scatter. Four misses across four different capabilities would be four weak spots; four misses of one habit is a single systematic gap, and it is the same shape as SE_MEM_007 - the principle was known and the confirming step was not run.

Chaining surfaced a defect no single drill can reach. The const-correctness drill asks for a cached length() with mutable members and the exception-safety drill asks for a mutex-guarded mutator; composed on one class they advertise thread safety for mutation while permitting a data race on a const read. Neither drill is wrong in isolation and the contradiction exists only in the composition.

Pricing copy-and-swap three ways corrected a loose framing carried in the drill's own wording. Against the copy-first ordering version it measured 0.93x over 200000 assignments of a 4 KB payload - no extra copy, both allocate one impl. Against an assignment that reuses the target's storage it measured 4.88x. The cost is real but is charged against a different alternative than the phrase extra copy implies.

Contamination declared and bounded: earlier in the same session the first roughly two hundred characters of four of the six Success Checks were printed while assessing whether the drills could share an artifact. observations: The attribution recorded in SE_EV_0045 was wrong and is corrected here. That entry reported four missed bullets and attributed them to six drills competing for attention on one artifact. Arm three chained the same six drills and passed all four, so composition did not cause them. The variable that mattered was a single sentence in the runner's instructions telling it that a described result is not a produced one. Arm one lacked that sentence and had every other advantage.

The four target bullets scored nought of four chained without the instruction, four of four singly with it, and four of four chained with it. The prediction that arm three would pass at least three was pre-registered before arm three ran, with the falsifier that two or more failures would make composition a real contributor.

All four Instructions asked explicitly for what their checks graded - mark every parameter and local, attempt to construct an invalid month, exercise both call forms and show each reaching the fast version, confirm no path leaves without releasing including early returns. This is not the shape repaired in f986590 where a check grades an artifact no step requests. The cards were sound and the runner skipped four explicit instructions.

The value of chaining is in the findings rather than the scores. Arm three produced six defects visible only because the drills shared a class, against one from arm one: the mutex must be excluded from the member swap or a held lock migrates to another object; the std::swap specialisation inherits noexcept(false) because the copy-assignment drill's user-declared copy constructor and destructor suppress the implicit moves, so it advertises a throwing swap for a body that cannot throw; copy assignment must invalidate the const-correctness drill's cache or a const length() returns the previous object's value forever; shared_ptr's deleter appears twice for two different obligations, releasing a lock and releasing memory; and two throw sites in one function forced a failure injector able to target the Nth construction. Arm three also reproduced arm one's finding that a mutable cache races with the mutex sitting beside it.

Three isolated runs converged on the same correction to the drill's own framing about copy-and-swap, and arm three refined it past arm one's measurement. For an lvalue source the extra cost is one Impl allocation rather than one Bitmap copy, and for an rvalue source it is zero through guaranteed elision into the by-value parameter rather than a move, since the class has no move constructor. Arm one's timing comparison of 0.93x missed the extra allocation because an Impl is small beside a four kilobyte bitmap copy.

Arm three caught a false positive in its own evidence. Its first copy-and-swap probe armed the failure globally, so the throw fired at the Impl copy and never reached the stream, producing a rolled-back object beside an unconsumed stream that would have supported a false claim of the strong guarantee. It rebuilt the harness to aim the failure at a chosen construction and reported the correct result, that the object is unchanged while the stream has advanced.

Both control runners independently reported what they had asserted rather than demonstrated, unprompted, arm two listing ten such items and arm three three. Arm two also found that the supplied build script failed under the PowerShell execution policy and needed a bypass flag, a defect in the controller's instructions rather than in the exercise.
